The *Mogharājattheraapadāna* is a verse narrative preserved in the *Therāpadāna* collection of the Pali Canon, recounting the past meritorious deeds and spiritual attainments of the elder Mogharāja [SuttaCentral]. According to SuttaCentral, translations of the text exist in five languages [SuttaCentral].

Textual reuse analysis by DharmaNexus highlights extensive links between this apadāna and the commentary on the *Theragāthā* (*Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*), which reproduces or shares long sequences of verses matching segments §1.1–20.3 and §13.3–15.2 [DharmaNexus]. Internal text sharing within the *Apadāna* collection occurs with a second poem dedicated to the same elder (*Mogharājattheraapadāna*, Tha-Ap 542, §20.1–22.1), as well as with poems for other disciples, including the *Bhāgineyyupālittheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 43), *Saparivārachattadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 332), *Cundattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 52), and *Sāgatattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 34) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus additionally generates automated cross-language alignments with Tibetan Mahāyāna texts, such as the *Kuśalamūlaparidhāra-sūtra* (D0101) and D0555, reflecting formulaic phrase matches rather than established historical parallels [DharmaNexus].
